clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs make the identical structural fix — splitting the single lock into a short-lived state lock plus a separate single-flight lock for refresh/auth transitions (`refresh_lock` in #2858, `flow_lock` in #3243), released before any HTTP request is yielded. #3243 goes further by also changing the primitive from `anyio.Lock` to `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)`, with an explicit comment that httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different async task than the one that acquired the lock — releasing an `anyio.Lock` from a different task than the one that acquired it raises a RuntimeError, a hazard `anyio.Semaphore` avoids since it isn't task-owned. #2858 keeps both locks as plain `anyio.Lock`, leaving that cross-task release hazard unaddressed.
